text: This website doesn't know your password.
When you sign up, a well-built site
runs your password through a hash:
a one-way function that turns it into fixed-length gibberish.
Change one letter, and the result changes completely.
It stores only the hash, plus a random salt,
When you log in, it hashes what you typed and compares.
Steal the database, and you get hashes, not passwords.
Weak ones can still be guessed, one hash at a time.
Follow. Tomorrow: why one terabyte shows nine hundred thirty-one gigabytes.
